summary.text:
Hart's Q2 Forecast pack (Cabinet 4 December 2025) is a 14-slide main deck plus three appendices — the treasury detail sits in Appendix 3, an 8-page mid-year review. Nothing distressed and the numbers are simple. The paper reports CFR £39.268m, external debt £13.711m and 'Under/(over) borrowing £25.557m' at the 25/26 estimate; identity CFR − external − OLTL (assumed zero, no line printed) reconciles exactly across all four forecast years.

The distinctive shape is on the balance sheet, not in the activity. Two PWLB loans against a £47.33m investment book — an investment-to-debt cover ratio of 3.45x and 65% of the CFR sitting internally (£25.6m). The gap doesn't close: forecast internal borrowing stays at £24.9m–£25.9m across all four years and the capital programme is entirely grant/reserve/revenue-financed with zero borrowing requirement.

The paper prints £285k interest payable on the £13.7m external debt line — an implied 2.051% weighted rate. Our bc-loans file holds two PWLB loans (1 ANNUITY, 1 MATURITY) totalling £13.624m at weighted 2.0502% — the rate ties to two decimal places, the principal is close but £87k off. Rate cross-check is quotable in the email; loan-count / principal tie is not.

Investment book at 30/9/25 has three LA counterparties (South Ayrshire, Hillingdon, Kingston-upon-Hull) totalling £19.5m or 41% of the book — Hart is a genuine lender in the LA-to-LA market, all three of those loans maturing between November 2025 and January 2026. MUFG interest-rate forecast dated 11 August 2025 shows Bank Rate path 4.00% → 3.50% by Sep-26 → 3.25% by Sep-27; forecast landed within 3-13bp of the actual PWLB curve on the day it was written, and its next testable point (Sep-26) is upon us.

No S151, no Contact Officer, no report-author block on any of the four PDFs — the main deck is a slide pack. Address is required before send. Draft is written and machine-checked.

officer.subject: £25.6m of your CFR is funded from your cash — and your book pays 2%
officer.body:
Hi [OFFICER],

Apologies for the cold email. PWLBtoday is fairly new so you may not have come across us yet.

We're built for local authority treasury teams and nothing else: live PWLB rates at both daily fixings, a monthly breakdown of every loan the sector draws, every council's PWLB book priced daily against the DMO's repayment curve, and a training academy for officers and members. There's more — the predictor, the SONIA path, peer metrics, a daily brief — in the brochure at [BROCHURE URL]. We don't sell treasury products, and the data side is free and stays free.

To keep that data and our training relevant we built tools that watch committee papers across every council in the country, so we can see how a council's own figures compare with where the market has gone since. So below are some thoughts on your Q2 Forecast pack from Cabinet on 4 December 2025. You're not being singled out — every authority gets one of these — and there's no agenda in it. The slide deck is unusually clear and the mid-year review in Appendix 3 is a compact treasury summary, so this is offered in that spirit, not as a critique.

The line that jumped out is the shape between your CFR and your external debt. Appendix 3 §6 walks CFR from £39.964m at 24/25 to £37.894m by 27/28, external debt from £14.079m to £12.951m, and 'Under/(over) borrowing' at £25.557m for 25/26 sits inside that. So about £25.6m of a £39.3m CFR — 65% — is funded internally from your own cash. That gap doesn't close across any of the four forecast years, and your three-year capital programme in Appendix 2 §17 is entirely grant, reserve and revenue-financed with a borrowing requirement of nought. It's an unusual shape for a district our library has read: most either sit closer to fully-external or are running the internal borrowing down as reserves get used.

The other observation is one your own numbers make. Section 12 of Appendix 1 prints £285k Interest Payable against the £13.7m external debt line — an implied weighted 2.05%. That's low against the certainty curve at any point since 2022 (30/09/25 was 4.58% at 1 year and 6.23% at 25 years — your own Appendix 3 §3). The dashboard at pwlbtoday.org/dashboard shows the certainty rate at each fixing today, and the 'your PWLB book' page prices Hart's book daily against the DMO's repayment curve — worth a look if it's ever useful for a scrutiny question about what the book is worth in market terms.

One dated piece from the paper worth a note. Your Appendix 3 §2 carries the 'MUFG Corporate Markets Interest Rate View 11.08.25' — Bank Rate to 3.75% by March 2026, 3.50% by September 2026, and 5-yr PWLB to 4.30% at Sep-26 with 10-yr to 4.80%. It landed within 3–13bp of the actual curve on the day it was written (that comparison sits inside your own tables on pp4–5), so it's a good baseline against which to test how much of the forward path has already moved. Every fixing since 30 September 2025 is on the platform, and the peer metrics page cuts other councils' current forecasts alongside it so you can see whether MUFG's view is still the sector consensus.

On training, three feel most relevant given the shape of your book: the liability benchmark pathway, which is interactive and built on live data — worth a look given where CIPFA is heading with the Prudential and Treasury Codes; interest rate risk, given the internal borrowing is essentially a rolling position between what your investment book earns (4-5% across most rows on slide 12) and what the external debt costs (the 2.05% implied above); and MRP policy, since your Appendix 1 §13 has MRP £15k over budget and there's no policy narrative in this pack to explain that. All 115 courses are free to local authorities until the end of September at pwlbtoday.org/academy.

And if you do find it useful, mentioning it to others would help us more than anything. We're small, word of mouth is most of our marketing, and every sign-up helps us prove the need.

Sign up free → https://pwlbtoday.org/
Follow on LinkedIn → https://www.linkedin.com/company/pwlbtoday/

Russell
https://www.linkedin.com/in/russelltew
